title: New webinar: Using flexible labor for the long term
summary: Instawork presents a new webinar discussing how long-term assignments for flexible workers can improve productivity and consistency in the workforce.
body_text: The key is consistency Sign up for our webinar on long-term use of flexible labor In roles where productivity is paramount, having experienced workers on the job for extended periods is often critical to success. Flexible workers are increasingly being used on a long-term basis to fill seasonal needs, support big projects, and fill in for permanent employees who take time off. There's also a growing emphasis on temp-to-hire, whereby flexible workers can audition for permanent positions via a long-term assignment. These long-term assignments can yield huge benefits. Rather than having a series of workers coming in to fill a staffing gap, a long-term assignment keeps training time to a minimum and raises the average level of experience on the floor. Experienced workers sourced from the flexible workforce are also a ready-made candidate pool for permanent positions. We're in SoCal! So how do businesses find the flexible workers who are ready to commit to a long-term assignment, and what's the best way to manage them for long-term success? We've assembled a panel of experts from among our business partners to discuss their experiences and offer their top tips. Come and here these leaders, along with our own Bryan Garcia, on April 9 at 1 pm EDT: Joey Bracco, Human Resources Business Partner, District Photo Joey has over a decade of comprehensive HR expertise, having led strategic initiatives at major corporations like Lowe's, Tractor Supply Company, and Walgreens. With a focus on talent acquisition, employee relations, and compliance Jared Heydari-Weatherly, Director of Operations, SPAR Group Jared Heydari-Weatherly has served as the Director of Operations for the Distribution Services division at SPAR Group, Inc., since September 2021. Jared oversees all operations for SPAR Distribution Services and has been working for the division since its infancy. Before joining SPAR, Jared had overseen the operations at many warehouse companies and has over 20 years of warehouse experience. Finding the right matches Looking for workers who can take on long-term assignments isn't quite the same as finding people for one-off, on-demand shifts. In this webinar, we'll take you through the process step-by-step, from recruitment to management and beyond: Preparing for long-term assignments How to design the assignment Planning training time and requirements Creating a candidate pool Setting the foundations for long-term success Onboarding flexible workers for long-term assignments Adjusting schedules and responsibilities on the fly Ensuring loyalty and retention Cementing the relationship Tracking productivity and creating a feedback loop Bringing back professionals for further assignments Selecting candidates for permanent roles You'll also have the chance to ask your own questions during our Q&A. If you're looking for more consistency in your workforce beyond your permanent employees, regardless of the industry you're in, then you'll be sure to come away with useful insights. Sign up today to reserve your place! Sign up for our webinar on long-term use of flexible labor

title: First United Bank & Trust Adopts Frederick Transit Stop Through Community Partnership Program
summary: First United Bank & Trust is proud to announce its participation in Frederick County Transit's Adopt-a-Stop Program through the adoption of the bus stop located on Riverbend Way in Frederick.
body_text: FREDERICK, Md. — First United Bank & Trust is proud to announce its participation in Frederick County Transit’s Adopt-a-Stop Program through the adoption of the bus stop located on Riverbend Way in Frederick. As part of this commitment, First United associates will help maintain the transit stop by conducting regular cleanups, monitoring the area for litter, and reporting any maintenance concerns to Transit Services of Frederick County. The Bank’s Riverside Office team will serve as the primary volunteers for the location and have committed to performing cleanups at least once each month. The Riverbend Way Stop is a highly visible transit location that features several rider amenities, including the overhead shelter, bench, trash receptacle, and solar lighting. “Supporting the communities we serve goes beyond banking,” said Nakisha Aviles-Broadnax, Regional Retail Manager at First United. “By adopting this bus stop, we’re investing in a shared community space by helping create a cleaner, safer, and more welcoming environment for residents and visitors who rely on public transportation every day. We believe these small acts of service can make a meaningful difference, and we’re excited to be part of this effort.” Frederick County Transit’s Adopt-a-Stop Program encourages businesses, civic groups, schools, and nonprofit organizations to take responsibility for one of the county’s nearly 400 bus stops and shelters. Participants help improve the appearance of transit facilities by removing litter, reporting graffiti or damage, and notifying Transit of any service-related concerns. In recognition of its commitment to the Adopt-a-Stop Program, First United has received a certificate of appreciation from Frederick County and a dedicated sign at the Riverbend Way bus stop. First United Corporation operates one full-service commercial bank, First United Bank & Trust. The Bank has a network of community offices in Garrett, Allegany, Washington, and Frederick counties in Maryland, as well as Mineral, Berkeley, and Monongalia counties in West Virginia. First United’s website can be located at MyBank.com. As of 6/30/2026, the corporation posted assets of $2.1 billion.

title: Connected Frontline Solutions Optimize Food Production Workflows
summary: Inside a bustling food and beverage facility, the smooth movement of materials dictates the pace of production. Any delay in getting raw ingredients to the line or moving finished goods to the warehouse creates a bottleneck.
body_text: Inside a bustling food and beverage facility, the smooth movement of materials dictates the pace of production. Any delay in getting raw ingredients to the line or moving finished goods to the warehouse creates a bottleneck. These intralogistics challenges are magnified in a labor-constrained environment, where an inexperienced workforce may struggle with manual, point-to-point material moves, leading to errors and production delays. The associated costs of these inefficiencies accumulate quickly. The High Cost of Intralogistics Inefficiency CBRE Supply Chain Advisory estimates that transportation and labor account for between 50% and 70% of total supply chain costs. Errors, such as loading incorrect materials, lead to expensive rework. Reducing product overfill by just 1% on a high-volume line can save approximately $500,000 per year. These financial pressures drive facility leaders to seek more efficient ways to manage their operations and staff. To overcome these hurdles, leading manufacturers focus on a strategy called the Connected Frontline (CFL). This approach integrates sensing technologies and advanced software to empower workers. It optimizes the flow of goods with real-time data. Zebra serves as the world’s foundation for intelligent operations. We design hardware, software, and automation solutions for the frontline and maintain decades of leadership in data capture solutions. Elevating Performance with a Connected Frontline A CFL strategy provides a base for intelligent operations by connecting workers, assets, and processes. Our vision sees frontline operations everywhere digitized, automated, and intelligent. Instead of relying on paper checklists, workflows shift to digital platforms. Imagine a low-stock alert from the Manufacturing Execution System. In a connected factory, this alert automatically triggers a task in an enterprise collaboration solution like Zebra Workcloud Task Management . The system assigns the task to the most appropriate forklift operator based on location and availability. It sends instructions directly to a mobile device . This provides real-time guidance to the worker for the correct material and drop-off point. Such digital methods optimize manual transport. Turning Real-Time Data into Targeted Action Connected Frontline strategies also depend on gaining real-time asset visibility . By automating data capture, managers get an accurate, up-to-the-minute view of all materials and work-in-process (WIP). A comprehensive RFID solution automates the tracking of goods as they move through the facility. This level of visibility enhances further with powerful communication and collaboration tools. A solution like Zebra Workcloud Sync unifies the frontline with Push-to-Talk (PTT) voice capabilities and secure messaging on a single device. A line worker can instantly contact a supervisor about a quality issue. A manager can broadcast instructions to the entire forklift team. This seamless flow of information eliminates silos, accelerates problem-solving, and ensures the entire operation moves in unison. Zebra relentlessly pursues innovation, focuses on customer commitment, and maintains a leading ecosystem. We believe the work we do each day makes work better every day for organizations and their employees. Our portfolio helps customers achieve real-time insight and optimized workflows. Reach out to our team to find a partner ready to support your business growth.

title: Lument Closes $28 Million HUD/FHA Multifamily Loan for the Acquisition and Rehabilitation of Ohio Affordable Housing
summary: The $28 million HUD/FHA 221(d)(4) loan supports TFG Housing Resources and Raise Up’s collaboration of the substantial rehabilitation of Western Horizon, preserving 353 affordable units in Lorain, Ohio.
body_text: The $28 million HUD/FHA 221(d)(4) loan supports TFG Housing Resources and Raise Up’s collaboration of the substantial rehabilitation of Western Horizon, preserving 353 affordable units in Lorain, Ohio. Columbus, OH— May 15, 2026 — Lument today announces the closing of a $28 million U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)/Federal Housing Administration (FHA) Section 221(d)(4) loan to assist TFG Housing Resources and Raise Up with the substantial rehabilitation of Western Horizon, a 353-unit affordable housing community in Lorain, Ohio. The transaction utilized a component of the Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program that allows for blending RAD with Section 18 of the National Housing Act to fund the preservation of aging affordable housing. Lument’s Joey Hague, managing director based in Columbus, led the transaction. “TFG Housing Resources is passionate about its mission to create quality affordable housing for families in need, and we are honored to help them advance their work,” said Hague. “The FHA 221(d)(4) program was an ideal fit as it installs fully amortizing 40-year construction to permanent financing at a favorable interest rate, positioning the community for future success.” The units were converted through the RAD program in conjunction with 4% low-income housing tax credits (LIHTCs) through the Ohio Housing Finance Agency. In addition to the FHA mortgage, Lument Securities served as the underwriter for $9.2 million in tax-exempt bonds. TFG Housing Resources is a Columbus-based real estate developer focused on the new construction and rehabilitation of affordable housing properties. Founded in 2023, it is associated with The Finch Group, which has a track record of more than 60 affordable housing developments and 10,000 units built. “Lument’s understanding of the complexities of utilizing the RAD program in conjunction with 4% LIHTC, along with its FHA expertise, made for an efficient process and optimal outcome,” said Brad Carman, president of TFG Housing Resources. “Their guidance was instrumental in navigating a transaction of this scale, which is one of the largest public housing renovations in Ohio’s history.” Originally built in the 1950s as three separate communities, Leavitt Homes, Westview Terrace, and Westgate Apartments have historically operated as public housing. As a result of the RAD conversion utilizing FHA financing, the properties now operate as one and are being rebranded as Western Horizon. Post renovation, all units will all be assisted by project-based rental assistance with rents restricted to 60% area median income (AMI). About Lument Lument, a subsidiary of ORIX Corporation USA, is a national leader in commercial real estate finance and delivers a comprehensive set of capital solutions customized for investors in multifamily, affordable housing, and seniors housing and healthcare real estate. Lument offers Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, FHA, USDA, and balance sheet financing, as well as a full suite of capital market lending products. In addition, Lument provides a suite of real estate advisory solutions including real estate investment sales, investment banking, and investment management solutions. The company has approximately 550 employees in over 25 offices across the United States. Securities, investment banking, and advisory services are provided through Lument Securities, LLC, member FINRA/SIPC. Lument Investment Management, LLC, is registered as an investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. For more information, visit https://www.lument.com/.

title: Digital sovereignty in Europe: why 7 out of 10 Spaniards are concerned about a concept they are not yet familiar with
summary: The Fundación Telefónica report reveals why digital sovereignty is a concern for citizens and businesses, and what this means for Europe.
body_text: Digital sovereignty in Europe: a growing concern, though still unfamiliar to many citizens Digital sovereignty has become a growing concern for European citizens and businesses, although it remains an unfamiliar term to a large part of the population. The report Digital Sovereignty in Europe 2026 , produced by the Telefónica Foundation, reveals a significant paradox: whilst only three in ten Spaniards say they are familiar with the concept, a large majority recognise the risks associated with dependence on foreign technology and call for greater European capacity to develop strategic technologies. The findings show a close link between digital sovereignty, security, trust, data protection, artificial intelligence and competitiveness. In a context where digital transformation is increasingly shaping the economy and everyday life, Europe’s ability to innovate, make decisions and compete technologically is emerging as one of the most important issues for its future. Imagine we keep our photos, our savings, our medical records and our chat conversations in a safe. We know it works well, but we do not know who holds the keys, under which laws it operates or what would happen if the rules of access were to change one day. In reality, something similar happens every day when we use apps, store information in the cloud, make digital payments or work with artificial intelligence tools. The issue is not whether these technologies are useful or not. The question is whether we have the capacity to make decisions about the technologies on which we increasingly depend. That, in essence, is the conversation about digital sovereignty. Interestingly, whilst the concept is still unfamiliar to a large part of the population, there is a growing awareness of its implications. The report Digital Sovereignty in Europe 2026 by Fundación Telefónica reveals a particularly interesting paradox: only 29 per cent of Spaniards say they have heard of this term, yet 82 per cent believe that Europe depends on technology companies from other countries and 86 per cent believe it should develop its own technologies to be more competitive. In other words, many citizens are unaware of the exact meaning of the concept, but they clearly perceive what it entails. And this perception cuts across the whole of society, regardless of age, gender, population size or professional activity. This tells us something important. Digital sovereignty is no longer a conversation reserved for experts, public officials or technology companies; it has become a matter of public interest, because technology is no longer merely a tool. It has become an essential infrastructure for the economy, education, healthcare, security and communications. Today we rely on telecommunications networks, data centres, cloud services, digital platforms, cybersecurity systems and artificial intelligence tools to carry out our daily activities and to keep organisations, businesses and institutions running. However, unlike other critical infrastructure, these are often invisible to most of us. We do not see the data centres where our information is stored. We do not usually ask ourselves who develops the algorithms we use every day. And even less so under which jurisdiction many of the digital services that form part of our daily routine operate. But we are becoming increasingly aware that these issues matter. The report’s data show that citizens do not perceive this dependence solely as a technological issue. There is a direct link to security, trust and decision-making. 62 per cent believe that dependence on foreign technology could pose a threat to European security. Furthermore, the areas causing the greatest concern are precisely those that will play a strategic role in the coming years, such as artificial intelligence and payment systems. It is not difficult to understand why. Technology is having an ever-greater influence on the decisions that affect our daily lives. Digital systems manage financial transactions, organise information flows, facilitate essential services and store personal and corporate data of immense value. That is why the discussion on digital sovereignty is closely linked to another key word: trust. The report shows that 90 per cent of Spaniards are concerned about large technology platforms’ access to banking information, 85 per cent about financial and tax data, and nearly 80 per cent about health or mobility-related information. We are not just talking about privacy. We are talking about who controls, manages and protects information that forms part of our personal and professional lives. We are talking about the ability of citizens and institutions to understand what happens to that data and under what rules it is used. The most interesting thing is that this concern does not imply a rejection of technology. Rather, it reflects the opposite. We are more connected than ever before. We use digital services constantly and recognise the enormous value they bring. Technology facilitates access to knowledge, improves productivity, connects people and opens up new economic and social opportunities. What seems to be emerging from this public consultation is a call for balance. A balance between innovation and trust, between openness and autonomy, between seizing the opportunities of digital transformation and retaining the ability to make decisions about it. Because digital sovereignty is not about disconnecting from the world. Nor does it involve erecting technological barriers or replacing one form of dependency with another. The fundamental question is whether Europe has sufficient in-house capabilities to innovate, compete and make decisions in strategic areas. In this regard, one of the most significant findings of the survey is that there is a clear willingness to support European alternatives. 70 per cent of citizens say they would choose a European platform if it offered the same features as a non-European one. This finding shifts the usual focus of the debate. We often discuss digital sovereignty from a perspective of concern: technological dependence, the gap with other regions or the loss of competitiveness. However, the results also point to an opportunity. Citizens not only identify a problem; they are also willing to back the solutions. The same signal is coming from the business sector. Spanish companies likewise perceive a high level of dependence on foreign technology and highlight artificial intelligence, cloud services, cybersecurity, data storage and digital platforms as areas where Europe should strengthen its capabilities. Furthermore, nine out of ten business leaders believe that European governments should actively promote the development of their own technology. When citizens and businesses agree so clearly on the diagnosis, it is evident that we are facing a structural issue. And this issue has a great deal to do with Europe’s future competitiveness. Because digital sovereignty is not just about technology. It is also about talent, education, research, industry, innovation, investment, ethics and the ability to transform knowledge into competitive solutions. It is about the possibility of developing technologies aligned with European interests and values. And, ultimately, it is about the ability to decide how we want to shape our digital future. Europe has significant strengths with which to tackle this challenge. It boasts world-class universities, leading research centres, advanced infrastructure, innovative companies and a strong tradition of protecting rights and fostering digital trust. The challenge seems to lie not so much in generating knowledge as in translating that knowledge into scale, innovation and technological leadership. It is precisely from this reflection that THINK&DO TECH was born, an initiative launched by the Telefónica Foundation to connect strategic thinking with the capacity for action around one of Europe’s greatest challenges: strengthening its own technological capabilities through a model that is competitive, reliable, scalable and aligned with European democratic values. The initiative is based on a simple idea: the debate on technological sovereignty will only be truly useful if it can be translated into collaboration, talent, partnerships and concrete projects. It therefore seeks to bring together experts, companies, institutions, researchers and civil society to develop a shared understanding of this challenge and identify opportunities for action that will help strengthen European technological autonomy. In line with Telefónica’s vision of driving people-centred digitalisation, this initiative reinforces an idea that is increasingly prominent in the European technological debate: innovation generates greater value when combined with trust, decision-making capacity and the development of sustainable and competitive digital ecosystems. The report’s findings show that there is growing concern about technological dependence, but also significant confidence in Europe’s ability to strengthen its position over the coming years. In fact, 54 per cent of Spaniards believe that European technological sovereignty will increase over the next decade. This is a reasonable level of optimism. Citizens recognise that the challenge exists, but they also perceive that Europe has significant assets to tackle it. The question no longer seems to be whether digital sovereignty should be part of the European agenda. The data indicate that it is already a concern for citizens and businesses. The question is how to respond to it. The key lesson from this listening exercise is that the conversation no longer revolves solely around technology. It revolves around the ability to make decisions. Deciding where our data is stored. Deciding which infrastructure we consider strategic. Deciding how we want to develop technologies that are critical to our economy and our society. Deciding which ethical and democratic values should be embedded in the digital tools that will have an ever-greater influence on our daily lives. Perhaps most people do not yet use the term ‘digital sovereignty’ in conversation. But that does not mean they do not care. The data shows precisely the opposite. And, although many may not yet be familiar with the term, an increasing number of citizens and businesses understand the question behind it: who holds the keys to the vast digital vault on which we all depend. And that may well be one of the most important discussions for the future of Europe. Our commitment is to help reduce this dependence in strategic areas by driving European competitiveness, innovation and leadership. In this context, at Telefónica we want to be the best gateway for citizens, businesses and institutions to access digital technologies, whilst strengthening Europe’s technological capabilities. Because digital sovereignty is not just a technological issue: it is also a matter of competitiveness, autonomy and the ability to decide the digital future we want to build. The question no longer seems to be whether digital sovereignty should be part of the European agenda. The data indicate that it is already a concern for citizens and businesses. The question is how to respond to it. The key lesson from this consultation exercise is that the conversation no longer revolves solely around technology. It revolves around the ability to make decisions. Deciding where our data is stored. Deciding which infrastructure we consider strategic. Deciding how we want to develop technologies that are critical to our economy and our society. Deciding which ethical and democratic values should be embedded in the digital tools that will have an ever-greater influence on our daily lives. Perhaps most people do not yet use the term ‘digital sovereignty’ in conversation. But that does not mean they do not care. The data show precisely the opposite. And, although many may not yet be familiar with the term, more and more citizens and businesses understand the question behind it: who holds the keys to the great digital safe on which we all depend. And that may well be one of the most important conversations for the future of Europe.

title: Accelerating the Next Era of AI: Celestica and AMD Collaborate on the AMD Helios Rackscale Solution
summary: Discover how Celestica and AMD are collaborating on the AMD Helios rackscale solution, featuring the high-performance DS6010 switch for next-gen data centers.
body_text: WRITTEN BY Matt Roman, Senior Director of Product Line Management share LinkedIn 2026-07-23 At Celestica, our core strength lies in combining world-class engineering, design, and manufacturing with a robust global supply chain to solve the most complex infrastructure challenges. This foundational capability is at the heart of our recent strategic collaboration with AMD to co-develop the open standards-based AMD Helios rackscale solution . AMD Helios pairs AMD high-performance computing leadership with Celestica's deep expertise in data center networking technology, this milestone partnership forms a new blueprint for next-generation data centers. Together, we are engineering solutions that seamlessly handle demanding workloads, reduce time-to-value, and improve supply chain resiliency across cloud, enterprise, and research environments. Optimized Switching Power: How the DS6010 Powers AMD Helios? Central to this question is the AMD/Celestica collaboration for AMD Helios and our new standard-setting product: the Celestica DS6010 networking switch , purpose-built for the AMD Helios. Engineered specifically for seamless integration within the AMD Helios architecture, the DS6010 is a 1-OU, cabled-backplane scale-up switch aligned with the Open Compute Project (OCP) Open-Rack-Wide (ORW) open standards. Operators and hyperscalers choose the DS6010 for its elite switching power: Massive Performance: It utilizes dual Broadcom Tomahawk 6 ASICs that deliver an astounding 204.8 Tbps of non-blocking capacity to easily handle extreme AI throughput. Ultra-Low Latency Interconnects: Features a high-density cabled backplane supporting high-speed 224G PAM4 SerDes to seamlessly interconnect up to 72 GPUs, which dramatically minimizes AI training latency and enables massive, efficient scaling. Plug-and-Play Integration: By offering the DS6010 as part of an integrated Helios rack-scale solution inside OCP ORW racks, it streamlines deployment and eliminates the challenges of complex data center integrations. Furthermore, operators gain complete peace of mind through automated cyber-resilience via Platform Firmware Resilience (PFR) which automatically detects and recovers from malicious firmware attacks. This is backed by a reliable hybrid liquid cooling design and 7+1 fan redundancy engineered for mission-critical uptime. Live at AMD Advancing AI 2026: See Our Innovations in Action We are incredibly excited to showcase these leading-edge solutions at the upcoming AMD Advancing AI 2026 conference from July 22–23 at Moscone West in San Francisco. Attendees have two premier opportunities to see how Celestica is changing the game: The AMD Instinct™ Showcase Area: Get an up-close, first-hand look at the groundbreaking DS6010 switch to witness its physical form-factor and advanced hybrid liquid-cooled layout. Celestica Booth #210: Drop by our main booth in the AI Expo Hall to learn the finer details of our strategic collaboration with AMD, explore our end-to-end platform solutions, and speak directly with our core engineering and product experts. Beyond the exhibition floor, our thought leaders will take center stage to deliver deep-dive technical insights: AI-Native Architecture Track: John Chiang (Director, Product Management, Network and Connectivity, Celestica) and Danny Moore (Director, AI Technology and Ecosystem Strategy, AMD) will present "Accelerating the Next Era of AI: Celestica Scale Up Switching for AMD Helios," exploring how high-speed switching eliminates infrastructure bottlenecks and optimizes large-scale AI clusters. Technical Deep Dive: Arun Solleti (Director Technical Marketing, Platform Solutions, Celestica) and AMD’s Chuck Gilbert (Sr. Director, Global Cluster Architecture and Design, AMD) will present "Architecting Open AI Fabrics: Scale-Out Network Fabrics for AMD Instinct™ Clusters with Celestica and SONiC," giving an exclusive technical breakdown of open standards for AMD Instinct MI300X and MI400X GPU clusters. Defining the Future: Celestica's Leadership in AI Switching Infrastructure Ultimately, our involvement in the AMD Helios project cements Celestica’s position as the go-to leader for high-performance, open, data center network infrastructure. From building strategic platform collaborations to scaling performance through our storage controllers (like the SC6100 and SC6110 with AMD EPYC™ processors) and AI Compute, we are paving the way forward. By continuously delivering market-leading networking switches —ranging from our 800G DS5000 to our 1.6T DS6001 and the massive 204.8T Helios scale-up DS6010—we take clear leadership of switch innovation in the high-performance AI market. We look forward to seeing you at AMD Advancing AI 2026 conference as we continue to accelerate real-world AI adoption. Visit Booth #210 or check out our event landing page to connect with an expert today! A 25+ year IT industry veteran, he brings deep expertise across AI, cloud, enterprise, and telecom sectors.
